title: A broadcast draft is not a send, scheduling one is not a send either, and cancelling is not an undo
summary: Three adjacent calls each look like they send mail and only one does. sendCreateBroadcast creates a draft; setting scheduled_at on it records INTENT and enqueues nothing, so an agent that composes + schedules and reports 'it will go out Monday' has sent nothing at all. sendQueueBroadcast is the single call that puts mail on the wire, and it is irreversible per row: sendCancelBroadcast abandons a broadcast that has not fanned out but deliberately does NOT withdraw rows already enqueued, so it is a stop-before-start, never an undo. The symmetric error is treating the queue response as a failure — already_enqueued>0 is a resumed idempotent fan-out and provider_configured:false is a deliberate dormant queue, while the real refusals are 422 no_audience, 422 no_sources and a 503 that must not be retried because suppression fails CLOSED.
references: app/api/v1/dashboard_send_broadcasts.py:174-185 create_broadcast — 'Creates a draft. Nothing is enqueued and no mail can leave until POST /{id}/queue'
app/api/v1/dashboard_send_broadcasts.py:224-233 cancel_broadcast — 'Already-queued rows are deliberately NOT withdrawn'
app/api/v1/dashboard_send_broadcasts.py:245-264 queue_broadcast — 202, already_enqueued is a RESUMED fan-out, provider_configured=false is a dormant state
app/schemas/send_broadcasts.py:148-151 scheduled_at — 'Hold fan-out until this instant', stored on the draft
